findings.title: Recovery codes stored under wrong field; user storage will keep a credential with null credentialData
findings.body: createRecoveryCodesCredential builds the input as `new UserCredentialModel("", credentialModel.getType(), recoveryCodesJson)`. The 3-arg `UserCredentialModel(String id, String type, String value)` constructor sets the `value` field and leaves `challengeResponse` as null (the parallel 4-arg constructor exists specifically to populate `challengeResponse`). The new BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential branch then reads `input.getChallengeResponse()`, so `recoveryCodesModel.setCredentialData(null)` is invoked and the JSON list of codes is silently dropped. Subsequent `getCredentials` will hit `JsonSerialization.readValue(null, List.class)` and the `isValid` branch will compare `input.getChallengeResponse()` against nothing, so the user can never authenticate with a recovery code stored in user storage. Either pass the JSON via the 4-arg constructor (e.g. `new UserCredentialModel("", type, recoveryCodesJson, null)`) or change the user storage provider to mirror OTP and use `input.getValue()` when populating `credentialData`. The added test testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin would fail today.

findings.title: Recovery codes read from challengeResponse instead of value
findings.body: The new `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE` branch stores the codes via `recoveryCodesModel.setCredentialData(input.getChallengeResponse())`. The credential is created in CredentialHelper with the 3-arg constructor, which populates `value`, not `challengeResponse`, so this field is null and the credentialData is never set. This is inconsistent with the OTP branch in the same method, which correctly reads `otpCredential.getValue()`. The branch should read `input.getValue()` (or, if challengeResponse semantics are desired, CredentialHelper must be changed to use the 4-arg constructor).

findings.title: NoSuchElementException if user has no recovery codes credential
findings.body: The bean calls `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel(credentialModelOpt.get())` without first checking `credentialModelOpt.isPresent()`. If the user no longer has a recovery-codes credential (e.g. the form is rendered while credentials are being recreated, after admin removal, or after `allCodesUsed()` already triggered `removeStoredCredentialById`), `Optional.get()` raises NoSuchElementException and the login page fails to render with a stack trace instead of a graceful error. A defensive null/empty check should be added (or the bean should not be instantiated when no credential is present).

findings.title: Used-up recovery codes will not be removed when stored in user storage
findings.body: When `recoveryCodeCredentialModel.allCodesUsed()` is true, the authenticator calls `authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())`. BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage implements only `CredentialInputUpdater` and `CredentialInputValidator`; it does not implement `CredentialProvider` and therefore has no `removeCredential` hook. The default Keycloak path for `removeStoredCredentialById` only delegates to `CredentialProvider` instances, so removal silently fails for a user-storage credential. The user is left with a credential whose codes are all used and the required action to reconfigure will be added, but the stale credential entry remains in user storage forever.

findings.title: disableCredentialType ignores recovery codes
findings.body: The override only clears OTP when `credentialType` matches an OTP type. When admin REST or the account console calls disable with `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE` (now advertised via `supportsCredentialType` and visible through `getCredentials`), the method just logs `Unsupported to disable credential of type` and returns. Either reject the type in `supportsCredentialType`/`getDisableableCredentialTypesStream`, or clear `myUser.recoveryCodes` like it does for OTP. Otherwise the admin can list and view recovery codes as disableable but never actually disable them.

findings.title: testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin does not verify code consumption
findings.body: The test only logs in once with one recovery code and then logs out. It does not verify that the used code is actually consumed (i.e. that a second login attempt with the same code fails and that subsequent use of an unused code works) and does not verify that when all codes are used the credential is removed and `CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES` is added. This leaves the most important behavioural guarantees of the new feature uncovered.

findings.title: getCredential javadoc is misleading
findings.body: The Javadoc says the method "Checks the user storage for the credential. If not found it will look for the credential in the local storage". The implementation actually chains `user.credentialManager().getFederatedCredentialsStream()` with `getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream(...)`. Whether user-storage credentials appear in `getFederatedCredentialsStream` is determined by the user storage provider implementing `CredentialProvider#getCredentials`; for providers that don't, this method will silently miss the federated credential. The doc should describe what `getFederatedCredentialsStream` is expected to return rather than asserting that all user storage providers will be hit.
